prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, art-direction paintover of an existing game location. Image 1 is a current in-game screenshot of the small car park on the top road of the Mega Park, a concrete skate park set into volcanic rock in the forest of an island in autumn, in the game Yorimichi. Its four realistic, photo-textured cars (a red sports coupe, a blue sedan, a white sedan and a silver SUV) do not fit the game. Image 2 is another place in the same game and shows the art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, simple chunky forms, indigo tiled roofs, autumn maples and ginkgos in rust, orange and gold, dark green pines, a clean blue sky. Repaint image 1 from exactly the same camera and composition as the improved AFTER version: the paintover a lead artist makes to show the team, concretely, what to build. The four cars are replaced by four small, friendly Japanese kei vehicles modelled in the game's own low-poly style, backed into the same four bays with their fronts toward the camera. From left to right: a sage-green kei pickup truck with a flat cab-over front, a cream roof and a drop-side bed carrying two wooden crates and a skateboard; a tall, boxy kei wagon in cream with an ochre lower body; a small, round retro kei car in vermilion with a cream roof and big round headlights; a one-box kei microvan in indigo with a white waist stripe and a roof rack carrying skateboards. Chunky, softly bevelled shapes, flat matte paint, simple dark windows, small black tyres with pale hubs, plain yellow number plates without characters. They are small: a little over three metres long and narrower than the bays, so concrete shows round them. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the concrete, the yellow bay lines, the low concrete wall, the rock, the bushes and the trees. Stay in the game's style; do not turn it photoreal. No logos, no people, no UI, no labels, no text.
